instruction: I am going on a camping trip with my siblings. I had sent out a checklist of things needed for the trip to them over email. See who has committed to bring what, and place an order on Amazon for the remaining items. Given the available choices pick the highest rated ones.
notes: The checklist is an email attachment (evaluation shows gmail.Attachment and file_system.File/Directory changes), so the plan finds the thread (inbox threads, query 'camping'), reads the thread to see which sibling committed to which item (commitments-known), logs into file_system, downloads the attachment and reads the file (checklist-known). The set of uncommitted items is only known at runtime; it is modeled with two placeholder product-type objects (remaining-type-1/2), each with a placeholder quantity and a placeholder 'top search result' product; candidate-product and checklist-quantity are structural slot associations, not prior knowledge. Each remaining type is searched with product_type filter and sort_by '-rating' and its first result is added to the cart with the checklist quantity. amazon.clear_cart is required before adding so the single order contains exactly the remaining items. place_order takes the two product types as non-API record parameters to force both items into the cart before ordering (equality used to force distinct types); its nullary effect order-placed is the only task-specific goal, so supervisor-complete-task needs no parameters. If more than two items remain at runtime, add further placeholder triples to the problem and extend place-order's precondition accordingly. Existing address/payment card are used (no address changes).
